lead.headline: A new COP31 draft admits for the first time that warming will pass 1.5C, but drops any direct mention of fossil fuels
lead.short: A new draft at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya would admit for the first time that global warming is on course to exceed 1.5C, while dropping any direct mention of fossil fuels. COP31 president Murat Kurum said the text could achieve consensus, and delegates reconvened on Sunday morning to approve it after running two days into overtime.

why.text: A deal that never names fossil fuels, the main driver of warming, would mark a retreat from the language countries agreed to two years ago.

more: The draft keeps language from an earlier COP that refers only to a transition away from oil, gas and coal, after producers led by Saudi Arabia pushed to drop any direct mention of fossil fuels. It calls for faster carbon-removal technology to eventually reverse the overshoot past 1.5C. "We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon," Kurum, who is also Turkey's environment minister, told a plenary session.

It was unclear whether every delegation had seen the wording overnight, leaving some countries only a few hours to raise objections before a session set for 07:00 GMT. France, Panama and small island states had fought through Friday night to keep stronger fossil fuel language in the deal; the summit, in Antalya, has now run two days past its scheduled close.

update.new: A new draft is out and reconvened for approval.
update.front: The COP has reached a near-final text after running into a second day of overtime, a genuine turn in a story that has run all week.

seconds.headline: Max Verstappen wins a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix with over 20 lead changes as the Ferraris collide
seconds.short: Max Verstappen held off George Russell and then Lando Norris to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix with more than 20 lead changes, his third win there in four years. Russell crashed out of second place with two laps to go, and Charles Leclerc collided with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton, who also took a 10-second penalty.

why.text: It was one of the most chaotic races of the year, and it ended Verstappen and Russell's running feud with a result, not just words.

more: Verstappen started from pole and traded the lead with Russell repeatedly in a slipstream-heavy race before Russell locked up trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second on lap 48 and hit the wall, dropping to ninth. Norris finished second and Oscar Piastri third. Leclerc was handed a 10-second penalty for spinning Hamilton, who had already taken his own penalty for gaining an advantage off track.

Afterwards Verstappen dismissed Russell's pre-race complaint that "somebody's got to stand up to" him: "He's so far below my level that it doesn't really bother me," he said. "Today, karma is a bitch." The pair had clashed in Friday's final practice. Formula 1 moves to Qatar next, with practice from Friday 27 November.

update.new: The race is run; Verstappen won it from pole.
update.front: A race this chaotic, with Parth's two F1 rivalries both settled on track, earns its place beside the day's bigger news.

seconds.headline: Mexico's military captures top drug lord "El Chapo Isidro" in a raid that sets off a gun battle
seconds.short: Mexican special forces, helped by US intelligence, captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro" and one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, in a raid in Sinaloa state on Friday night. The operation set off a gun battle that caused panic in the city of Guasave; two other alleged cartel leaders were also arrested.

why.text: He evaded capture for more than a decade despite a $5m reward, and Mexico's government has named him a leader of a second major cartel.

more: The FBI's wanted poster says Meza Flores's organisation is responsible for moving heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States. Mexico's defence ministry also alleges he leads the Beltran Leyva criminal organisation, allied to the Mayos faction of the Sinaloa cartel. His alleged second-in-command, known as "Serafin", and an alleged financial operator were arrested alongside him.

The raid was carried out by elite military forces after they moved into the target area using stealth and surprise, Mexico's defence ministry said. Eleven people were killed in the violence that followed across Guasave as the operation unfolded, according to Mexican officials.

stories.headline: Nine members of a family returning from a pilgrimage are killed when their vehicle hits a parked truck in Rajasthan
stories.short: Nine members of a family from Maharashtra's Dhule district, returning from the Khatu Shyamji temple, were killed when their vehicle rammed a truck parked on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan's Kota district early Sunday, police said. Eight others travelling with them were injured. A preliminary probe suggests the driver may have fallen asleep.

why.text: A single family lost nine members, including children, in one accident on a highway known for such crashes.

more: The MUV was carrying 16 members of two brothers' families when it struck the parked truck at around 1am, superintendent of police Tejeshwani Gautam said. Nine people, including women and children, died at the scene; eight others were admitted to hospital. Additional district collector Rajesh Joshi said the group was travelling home to Dhule after visiting Khatu Shyam.

President Droupadi Murmu condoled the deaths in a post on X, calling the accident "extremely saddening". Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately announced ex gratia payments from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund for families hit by a second deadly crash the same night, in Gujarat's Kutch district.

stories.headline: Seven people from two Army families, including three children, are killed in a head-on crash in Gujarat's Kutch
stories.short: Two Army personnel, their wives and three young children, all from Uttarakhand's Garhwal region, were killed when their car was split in two in a head-on collision with a trailer truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway in Gujarat's Kutch district on Saturday night, police said. The families had travelled to Kutch to see the Rann.

why.text: Two serving soldiers posted in Bhuj lost their wives and children alongside them, on a trip meant to be a holiday.

more: The car collided with the truck between 9.30pm and 10pm as it travelled from Khavda towards Bhuj, Kutch (West) superintendent of police Vikas Sunda said. All seven occupants, named as Saurabh Singh Negi, his wife Savita and their three-month-old daughter Sivika, Rajesh Singh Rawat and his seven-year-old daughter Rakshita, and Rinki Nitin Gosai and her four-year-old daughter Vamika, died of their injuries.

Negi and Rawat were serving in the Army and posted in Bhuj. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced compensation of ₹2 lakh for each deceased's next of kin and ₹50,000 for the injured from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund, and said he was praying for a speedy recovery for those hurt.

briefs.headline: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joins the BJP as a special invitee to its OBC Morcha executive committee
briefs.text: Chahal, who will represent Delhi on the panel, thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah in a post on X after the appointment was announced on Saturday. He had earlier met the OBC Morcha's national president, Rajya Sabha MP Amarpal Maurya.

briefs.headline: Pakistan's minister invokes Ghalib and Mughal history at an SCO forum held at Delhi's Purana Qila
briefs.text: Musadik Malik, addressing the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Urdu, invoked the Mughal emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, both linked to the fort's construction, calling it a story of overlapping history. The three-day summit was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday.

stories.headline: Masked ICE agents drag two people away on a crowded Seattle airport jet bridge, delaying a flight
stories.short: Masked immigration officers detained two people on a jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma airport as passengers were boarding on Saturday, a scene the airline called "distressing". Video showed officers dragging a man away as a woman screamed that her daughter was being taken; another passenger threw hot coffee on the officers and now faces a federal charge.

why.text: Enforcement at an airport gate, filmed and shared widely, has become one more flashpoint in Trump's immigration crackdown.

more: ICE said its officers were carrying out a targeted operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who had overstayed his visa. The woman who threw coffee, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, was also found to be in the country illegally and could be charged with assaulting a federal officer, ICE said in its statement on the arrests.

Alaska Airlines said ICE gave no advance notice of the operation, which delayed its Los Angeles-bound flight 1306 on a busy pre-Thanksgiving travel weekend. The airline said it was "concerned" by the scene on its jet bridge. Washington's governor and a union representing airport workers condemned the arrests, and video of the detentions spread quickly online.

stories.headline: A Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad is hit by a drone and drifts into Finnish waters
stories.short: The Sparta II, a Russian cargo ship linked to Moscow's defence ministry, caught fire after a drone strike in the eastern Gulf of Finland on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Finland's defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, and Finland's prime minister said the war was "spilling over" into the country's immediate vicinity.

why.text: A strike this close to Finland, a NATO member since 2023, shows the war reaching waters the alliance patrols.

more: Kaliningrad's governor said two drones had been used and that there was "no threat" to the exclave's supplies. The Sparta II, under US and Ukrainian sanctions since 2022, is run by a Russian firm that says on its website it was set up within the defence ministry's structure in 2011. Kyiv has not commented.

Finland's coast guard said it was alerted at about 08:50 local time and located the ship roughly 50km west of Suursaari island, prompting temporary aviation and maritime restrictions. Finland's defence ministry separately said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace shortly after the strike.

stories.headline: Gold has fallen 31% and silver 64% since their January peaks, cutting a ₹10 lakh investment to about ₹6.85 lakh
stories.short: Gold has fallen 31.5% and silver 64.2% from their January highs, after both metals surged to record prices and then corrected sharply through the year. A ₹10 lakh investment made at gold's January peak would be worth about ₹6.85 lakh now, and the same sum in silver about ₹3.58 lakh, Livemint calculated from the latest prices.

why.text: Investors who bought near the top, including those in gold ETFs, have lost more than a quarter of their money in ten months.

more: The IBJA's rate for 24K gold touched a fresh low of ₹1,23,890 for 10 grams on Thursday, down 13.2% in a month and 8.8% in a week, as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve and a broader pullback from safe-haven assets weighed on prices through November.

Gold had surged past ₹1,62,154 for 10 grams in August, its high for the year, before the slide began. Silver's fall has been steeper still, more than reversing a rally that had drawn in retail investors through the first half of the year. Investors who bought near the top, including those holding gold exchange-traded funds, have seen more than a quarter of their money wiped out in ten months.

update.new: Gold has fallen further to a fresh low, and the cumulative loss since January is now counted.

briefs.headline: CII proposes 15 financial sector reforms to the government's new committee on banking for Viksit Bharat
briefs.text: The industry body's proposals include a rule-based liquidity window for well-governed NBFCs, a wider investor base for lower-rated corporate bonds and a national catastrophe risk pool. The committee, announced in the Union budget, must share its recommendations within six months.

briefs.headline: Meta's AI chief Alexandr Wang needles Apple days after praising its CEO for "great doing business"
briefs.text: Replying to a rumour that Apple is building an AI agent similar to Meta's Muse, Wang wrote that the company is about to "unleash yet another" disappointing product. Days earlier he had thanked Apple CEO John Ternus for a partnership between the two companies.

briefs.headline: The Japanese-European BepiColombo probe enters orbit around Mercury after an eight-year, 10-billion-km journey
briefs.text: The European Space Agency said the spacecraft, launched in 2018, fired its thrusters for more than half an hour to achieve orbital capture around the Solar System's smallest and least understood planet. ESA's mission chief has said the probe will give "never-before-seen views" of Mercury.

briefs.headline: Arsenal escape with a draw at Newcastle after losing goalkeeper David Raya to a shoulder injury
briefs.text: Pedro Neto's early goal put Newcastle ahead before Noni Madueke's second-half equaliser rescued a point for Arsenal, who stay top of the Premier League. Raya, Arsenal's first-choice goalkeeper, went off with what the club called a potentially significant injury.

briefs.headline: Evanilson scores for a sixth straight league game as Bournemouth beat Nottingham Forest for a ninth win in a row
briefs.text: The Brazilian forward's 19th-minute strike set up a 2-0 win that lifted Bournemouth to fourth place in the Premier League. Forest's defeat leaves them above the relegation zone only on goal difference, despite their win over Manchester City before the international break.

briefs.headline: Debinha's stoppage-time strike gives Kansas City Current their first NWSL title, 2-1 over Washington Spirit
briefs.text: Vanessa DiBernardo's direct corner and a Debinha stoppage-time strike gave Kansas City the win at Audi Field; Trinity Rodman's 98th-minute header for Spirit came too late. It ended Rodman's bid to avoid a third straight final defeat.

update.new: They have now won the title.

briefs.headline: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami are on the brink of an early MLS playoff exit after a 3-0 loss to Columbus
briefs.text: Messi was shown a yellow card for throwing a ball into an opponent's face as 10-man Miami fell behind in the first leg of their playoff tie. Columbus coach Laurent Courtois said Messi should have been sent off; the referee disagreed.

stories.headline: Real Madrid come from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Bernabeu, their ninth straight win
stories.short: Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at home after Pablo Duran's early goal and a missed Kylian Mbappe penalty put them behind. Jude Bellingham equalised in the 66th minute, and substitute Carlos Espi scored the winner in the 85th from a Vinicius Junior cross, extending Madrid's winning run to nine matches in all competitions.

why.text: Madrid needed a substitute's goal to stay perfect at home and keep pace with Barcelona, level on points at the top of La Liga.

more: Thibaut Courtois made two outstanding saves to keep the comeback alive, the biggest after Bernardo Silva gave the ball away with Celta already ahead; Kylian Mbappe had earlier blazed a first-half penalty over the crossbar that would have levelled the scores sooner. Arda Guler's move into a deeper midfield role in the second half gave him more time on the ball and helped Madrid work through Celta's press, and Vinicius Junior's introduction from the bench set up the winner.

Espi, who struck his fourth goal of the season, said the Bernabeu atmosphere gave him "goosebumps" after his rebound sealed the win and stressed the squad's unity. Madrid, who stay second in La Liga level on points with leaders Barcelona, turn to the Champions League on Tuesday, when they host PSV at the Bernabeu in their fifth group match.

briefs.headline: Rafael Nadal is elected to Real Madrid's board of directors with 99.5% of the vote
briefs.text: The tennis legend, an honorary club member since 2011, becomes the board's 19th member after 1,704 of 1,713 votes cast at the general assembly backed him. "This club connects me with family and friends," Nadal said in a statement.

briefs.headline: Rishabh Pant's 128 takes India to a declared 720 for 9 as New Zealand trail by 233 in Wellington
briefs.text: Pant's century, his first in New Zealand, anchored India's innings before the declaration left New Zealand needing to bat out the final day to save the first Test. It is India's highest Test total of the year.

update.new: India have now declared at 720/9, with Pant's century the highlight.

briefs.headline: Carlos Alcaraz will face Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals title decider in Turin
briefs.text: Alcaraz recovered from a set down to beat Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1), dominating the tie-break 7-1 despite strapping on his injured hamstring. It is his second straight ATP Finals final, after losing to Jannik Sinner there last year.

update.new: He has now beaten Shelton to reach the final.

briefs.headline: BESCOM schedules power cuts of up to 12 hours across 127 Bengaluru areas on Monday for maintenance
briefs.text: Areas near the Pottery Road substation face the longest outage, from 9am to 7.30pm, while zones near Nandini Layout and the Sarakki and Adugodi sub-stations lose power for shorter stretches. BESCOM has asked residents to plan around the schedule.

briefs.headline: Twenty flights are cancelled and four diverted at Ranchi airport as Cyclone Akvan cuts visibility
briefs.text: Visibility at Birsa Munda Airport fell to about 1,000 metres against the 1,200 to 1,500 metres needed for safe landings, the airport director said. Jharkhand had cloudy weather and light rain since Friday; conditions were expected to improve from Sunday.

briefs.headline: Prayagraj starts building pontoon bridges for the 2027 Magh Mela, on a ₹200 crore budget
briefs.text: Workers have begun a VIP-area pontoon bridge and sand roads along the Sangam ahead of the bathing festival, due to begin on 14 January. The fair will eventually have nine pontoon bridges and 35 bathing ghats, officials said.

briefs.headline: Prayagraj will build three bus terminals on its outskirts to keep outstation buses out of the city centre
briefs.text: The terminals will come up at Kanihar, near Leprosy Crossing and at Phaphamau, serving buses from Varanasi, Chitrakoot and Lucknow respectively. The municipal corporation has identified land at all three sites and will send a proposal to the roadways department.

briefs.headline: Prayagraj police register an FIR over violence in an Allahabad High Court courtroom last month
briefs.text: The FIR, invoking 12 sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, follows a complaint from the High Court's registrar after alleged vandalism in Court No. 49 on 28 October. The accused are listed as unknown.
